title: Functor and transformation descent without identity-normalized stage transitions
statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preorder, and let $S=(C_i,T_{ij},a^C_{ijk})$ and $S'=(D_i,U_{ij},a^D_{ijk})$ be stage systems and $P_C,P_D$ their literal pair categories [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. Only the associative pentagon is assumed: no unitor or identity normalization of $T_{ii}$ or $U_{ii}$ is required. Write $j_i^C,j_i^D$ for the stage inclusions. Composition below is read from right to left.

Suppose functors $\Phi_i:C_i\to D_i$ and natural isomorphisms $b_{ij}:U_{ij}\Phi_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi_jT_{ij}$ are given for all $i\le j$. Assume, for every $i\le j\le k$ and $x\in C_i$,
$$\Phi_k(a^C_{ijk,x})\circ b_{jk,T_{ij}x}\circ U_{jk}(b_{ij,x})=b_{ik,x}\circ a^D_{ijk,\Phi_i x}.$$
Then there is a functor $\overline\Phi:P_C\to P_D$ with literal object formula $\overline\Phi(i,x)=(i,\Phi_i x)$ and representative formula
$$\overline\Phi[m,u]=[m,b_{jm,y}^{-1}\circ\Phi_m(u)\circ b_{im,x}],\quad u:T_{im}x\to T_{jm}y.$$
There are natural inclusion comparisons $\overline\Phi j_i^C\cong j_i^D\Phi_i$ with identity components, so the two functors agree on stage arrows.

For a second such family $(\Psi_i,c_{ij})$, suppose natural transformations $\eta_i:\Phi_i\Rightarrow\Psi_i$ satisfy
$$c_{ij,x}\circ U_{ij}(\eta_{i,x})=\eta_{j,T_{ij}x}\circ b_{ij,x}.$$
Their components $j_i^D(\eta_{i,x})$ define a natural transformation $\overline\eta:\overline\Phi\Rightarrow\overline\Psi$. Descent preserves identities and vertical composition of these transformations and hence their equations and inverses. The family $\Phi_i=1_{C_i}$, $b_{ij}=1_{T_{ij}}$ descends to the identity functor through a natural comparison with identity components. For a third stage system $S''=(B_i,V_{ij},a^B_{ijk})$ on $I$ and a coherent family $\Gamma_i:D_i\to B_i$, $d_{ij}:V_{ij}\Gamma_i\cong\Gamma_jU_{ij}$ satisfying the analogous tower equation, the family $\Gamma_i\Phi_i$ with comparisons $\Gamma_j(b_{ij,x})\circ d_{ij,\Phi_i x}$ descends to $\overline\Gamma\,\overline\Phi$ through a natural comparison with identity components. These statements include repeated indices and impose no faithfulness or exactness condition on transitions.

proof.text: Use the pair-category representatives, transport, identities and inclusions of [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. Put $B_m(u)=b_{jm,y}^{-1}\Phi_m(u)b_{im,x}$ for $u:T_{im}x\to T_{jm}y$. For $n\ge m$, abbreviate $A_i=a^C_{imn,x}$, $A_j=a^C_{jmn,y}$, $D_i=a^D_{imn,\Phi_i x}$ and $D_j=a^D_{jmn,\Phi_j y}$. The assumed tower equation, multiplied on the right by $D_i^{-1}$, reads $b_{in,x}=\Phi_n(A_i)b_{mn,T_{im}x}U_{mn}(b_{im,x})D_i^{-1}$; the same formula holds for $j,y$. No identity normalization is used in this rearrangement.

proof.text:
Substitute those two expressions in $B_n(A_jT_{mn}(u)A_i^{-1})$ and cancel $\Phi_n(A_j)$ and $\Phi_n(A_i)^{-1}$. The result is
$$D_jU_{mn}(b_{jm,y}^{-1})b_{mn,T_{jm}y}^{-1}\Phi_n(T_{mn}(u))b_{mn,T_{im}x}U_{mn}(b_{im,x})D_i^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $b_{mn}$ gives $b_{mn,T_{jm}y}^{-1}\Phi_n(T_{mn}(u))b_{mn,T_{im}x}=U_{mn}(\Phi_m(u))$. Thus the displayed expression is $D_jU_{mn}(B_m(u))D_i^{-1}$, exactly the transport of $B_m(u)$ in the target pair category [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. If two representatives become equal at an upper stage, their images become equal at that same stage by this equality. Consequently $[m,u]\mapsto[m,B_m(u)]$ is well defined on the stated equivalence classes.

proof.text: Give the descended functor the stipulated object function. Since $B_i(1_{T_{ii}x})=b_{ii,x}^{-1}1b_{ii,x}=1$, it preserves the prescribed identity representative [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. At a common stage $m$ for composable $u,v$, cancellation of $b_{jm,y}b_{jm,y}^{-1}$ gives $B_m(v)B_m(u)=b_{km,z}^{-1}\Phi_m(vu)b_{im,x}=B_m(vu)$. Directedness supplies a common upper stage for any two given representatives; step 2 permits replacing them by their transports there. The composition formula in the cited definition therefore proves preservation of every composite. These checks construct the functor, including its representative formula.

proof.text: For $f:x\to y$ in $C_i$, naturality of $b_{ii}$ gives $b_{ii,y}^{-1}\Phi_i(T_{ii}(f))b_{ii,x}=U_{ii}(\Phi_i(f))$. The inclusion formula in [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data] now gives $\overline\Phi(j_i^C(f))=j_i^D(\Phi_i(f))$, while the object functions literally agree. The identity at each common object consequently gives a natural inclusion isomorphism with identity components, in the orientation of the statement. This calculation uses $b_{ii}$ as supplied; it never replaces that isomorphism or $T_{ii}$ by an identity.

proof.text: For any stage arrow $f:x\to y$ and $i\le m$, naturality of $a^D_{iim}$ gives $a^D_{iim,y}U_{im}(U_{ii}(f))(a^D_{iim,x})^{-1}=U_{im}(f)$. Hence the inclusion arrow $j_i^D(f)$ has representative $[m,U_{im}(f)]$ by the transport and inclusion definitions [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. In particular the proposed transformation component at $(i,x)$ is represented at any $m\ge i$ by $U_{im}(\eta_{i,x})$. This establishes the common-stage component formula needed for naturality, also when $m=i$.

proof.text: Identity transformation families satisfy compatibility because $b_{ij}U_{ij}(1)=1b_{ij}$. If $\lambda:\Psi\Rightarrow\Omega$ has comparisons $e$, then $e_{ij}U_{ij}(\lambda_i\eta_i)=\lambda_jT_{ij}\,c_{ij}U_{ij}(\eta_i)=\lambda_jT_{ij}\,\eta_jT_{ij}\,b_{ij}$, so vertical composites are compatible. At $(i,x)$ their descended component is $j_i^D(\lambda_{i,x}\eta_{i,x})=j_i^D(\lambda_{i,x})j_i^D(\eta_{i,x})$; identities are handled by the same inclusion functor [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. Equality of transformation families therefore gives equality of descended components. If $\eta_i$ are invertible, rearranging compatibility gives $b_{ij}U_{ij}(\eta_i^{-1})=(\eta_jT_{ij})^{-1}c_{ij}$; the descended inverse has both inverse equations by the just-proved identity and composition formulas.

proof.text: For the identity family its tower equation is the equality $a^C_{ijk}=a^C_{ijk}$. Its arrow formula is $1^{-1}1(u)1=u$ at every stage. Hence its descent has the identity object and arrow functions, so identity components give the claimed natural comparison [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data].

proof.text:
For the composite family put $e_{ij,x}=\Gamma_j(b_{ij,x})d_{ij,\Phi_i x}$. It is a natural isomorphism since both factors are. Here is its tower calculation (arguments not displayed are the uniquely typed ones at $x$):
$$e_{ik}a^B=\Gamma_k(b_{ik})\Gamma_k(a^D)d_{jk,U_{ij}\Phi_i x}V_{jk}(d_{ij})
=\Gamma_k\Phi_k(a^C)\Gamma_k(b_{jk,T_{ij}x})\Gamma_kU_{jk}(b_{ij,x})d_{jk,U_{ij}\Phi_i x}V_{jk}(d_{ij})
=\Gamma_k\Phi_k(a^C)\Gamma_k(b_{jk,T_{ij}x})d_{jk,\Phi_jT_{ij}x}V_{jk}(\Gamma_j(b_{ij,x}))V_{jk}(d_{ij})
=\Gamma_k\Phi_k(a^C)e_{jk,T_{ij}x}V_{jk}(e_{ij,x}).$$
The first equality is the tower equation for $d$, the second is that for $b$, and the third is naturality of $d_{jk}$ at $b_{ij,x}$. Thus steps 1-3 apply to this coherent family. Expanding its representative formula gives
$$e_{jm,y}^{-1}\Gamma_m\Phi_m(u)e_{im,x}=d_{jm,\Phi_jy}^{-1}\Gamma_m(b_{jm,y}^{-1}\Phi_m(u)b_{im,x})d_{im,\Phi_ix},$$
which is exactly the successive representative formula for $\overline\Gamma\,\overline\Phi$. Objects also agree literally; identity components therefore define the final natural comparison [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. All displayed equations permit repeated indices and use only functoriality, naturality, and inverse cancellation.
